tldr: Headline coverage is almost entirely locked on a single register: the Pentagon's own watchdog confirming a US munitions shortfall from the Iran war, a disclosure that contradicts months of White House denials. Al Jazeera is the sole outlier, inverting the dominant shortfall frame toward Iranian strike effectiveness — leading with 'dozens of aircraft, hundreds of buildings' destroyed — while wire services and French-language outlets are the only ones whose homepage headlines also carry the Iran-US diplomatic breakdown, a thread visible to RSS readers of those outlets but invisible to readers of any other.

single_outlet_findings.finding: The only headline in the corpus to lead with Iranian strike effectiveness rather than the US munitions shortfall — 'Dozens of aircraft, hundreds of buildings: US loss to Iran attacks revealed' — inverting the accountability frame toward an Iranian-capability frame that no other outlet adopted at headline level.

Only headline to name Trump explicitly in an accountability formulation ('despite Trump's claims...defence officials confirm') while simultaneously citing the $33.4bn war cost — the sole title that combines the political-contradiction and economic-cost angles in a single headline.

The headline 'War on Iran resulted in munitions shortfall for US' frames the US as the aggressor ('war on Iran') rather than a party to a war with Iran — a framing choice absent from every other English-language title in the corpus.

bottom_line: At headline level, the Pentagon watchdog's munitions-shortfall disclosure dominates 10 of 11 regional buckets almost identically, with Al Jazeera as the only outlier redirecting readers toward Iranian strike damage rather than US supply vulnerability.
